headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading errors: CrewAI can read/write the workspace and send data to model providers while Airbyte broadly egresses business data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and uses stdin/stdout plus browser/tool integrations, so attacker-controlled files or outputs can be reinterpreted as instructions. Airbyte can move business data through APIs and broad egress, creating a plausible bridge if its outputs are fed into CrewAI. No shared MCP is shown, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into CrewAI prompts or files in the shared working directory
IF CrewAI agents treat file or stdout content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents into prompts
Add a provenance tag to all Airbyte outputs
Require manual review before CrewAI acts on any imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; CrewAI reads the filesystem, writes the filesystem, and sends data to model providers and tool integrations. In default setups, shared workspace content can flow from Airbyte into CrewAI and then out to third parties, so sensitive business data can leak without explicit user intent.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into a workspace CrewAI can read
IF CrewAI forwards that workspace content to model providers or external tools
mitigations: Use separate non-shared workspaces
Restrict CrewAI to redacted inputs only
Block outbound network except approved endpoints
Rotate and scope API keys used by CrewAI
Run a quick data-flow audit before enabling both together

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and has broad egress, while CrewAI can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, write the filesystem, and use browser/tool integrations. Their write and network capabilities overlap on shared mutable resources, so concurrent modification or race conditions are plausible even though CrewAI does not modify git state by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working directory or shared API-backed resource
IF CrewAI subprocesses and Airbyte jobs run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories or buckets
Serialize jobs with a simple lock file
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources
Limit CrewAI to read-only access where possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing, shared-memory design can treat upstream outputs as authoritative, and it can act through tools or subprocesses. Airbyte produces data-pipeline outputs that CrewAI may consume; if those outputs are wrong or poisoned, CrewAI can propagate them into downstream actions. The pair therefore supports a default cascade from data ingestion to action-taking.
conditions: IF CrewAI uses Airbyte outputs as task context without verification
IF CrewAI tools or subprocesses act on those outputs
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action
Require schema validation on Airbyte outputs
Mark upstream data as untrusted in CrewAI prompts
Log and review any tool action derived from imported data

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data plus API keys for tools and model providers. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out; uncertainty escalates to medium because the pair can move regulated data through external model providers and APIs by default.
conditions: IF regulated business data is passed from Airbyte into CrewAI
IF CrewAI sends that data to external model providers or tools
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it to CrewAI
Keep regulated data out of CrewAI prompts
Confirm residency and retention settings for all providers
Document a deletion/export workflow for both systems
